project.name: DBLocal
project.description: Rust desktop app that installs and manages local database servers (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Valkey) with several versions side by side, without containers and without sudo.
project.coreValue: Multi-version native, one click, no container
project.firstSessionJob: One running instance + the connection URI copied in < 2 minutes
project.licenseNotes: Every dependency must be GPL-compatible (Apache-2.0, MIT, ISC, SQLite public domain), enforced by the cargo deny allowlist. DBDelve code is not copied — an engineering decision, not a licensing limitation (DBDelve is GPL-3.0 too).
nonGoals: In-app data browsing/query (the DB client's territory)
Server/headless mode or a system service
Adopting an existing database install on the machine

phases.name: Spikes & Foundation
phases.goal: Prove the three riskiest assumptions (cross-OS GPUI, the Valkey Windows build, the GPUI tray) before writing product code
phases.definitionOfDone: Five spikes documented with YES/NO answers; the D-13 and D-04 decision gates run on failure; workspace + CI matrix green

phases.name: MVP Vertical Slice
phases.goal: A developer can install DBLocal, run PostgreSQL or Valkey, and use it for a real project
phases.definitionOfDone: On five OS targets: download -> create -> start -> copy URI -> connect succeeds; TTFRI PostgreSQL p50 < 120s measured in CI; the instance survives an app quit; AppImage/.tar.gz/.dmg (notarized)/.zip + install.sh ship with checksums

phases.name: MySQL family, CLI & native packages
phases.goal: The four-engine promise is met, and DBLocal works without a terminal as well as from inside one
phases.definitionOfDone: MySQL & MariaDB pass the same E2E as Phase 1; a project database can be created entirely from the GUI; the CLI is complete with --json and exit codes; .deb/.rpm/.msi ship; self-update works and is disabled for package-manager installs

phases.name: Configuration, autostart & polish
phases.goal: DBLocal becomes part of the daily routine and can be tuned without opening a configuration file
phases.definitionOfDone: A configuration form for all four engines with automatic recovery; user-level autostart on three OSes that can be cleanly revoked; the accessibility checklist passes

deployment.choice: GitHub Actions matrix + GitHub Releases + install.sh (curl)

extras.secrets: keyring (Secret Service / Keychain / Credential Manager) + 0600 file fallback
extras.async: tokio on a separate thread, never on the GPUI executor
extras.signing: Apple Developer ID + notarization (mandatory); Windows unsigned in v1

engines.binarySource: download.valkey.io for Linux; our own CI build for macOS & Windows (depends on F-SPK-02)

subFeatures.name: GPUI runs on three OSes
acceptanceCriteria: Given a Linux CI runner with a Vulkan driver, When the spike binary runs, Then a GPUI window opens and renders a list plus buttons from gpui-component, then exits with code 0
Given a Linux machine without Vulkan, When the binary runs, Then the app exits with an actionable message (naming the driver packages + a documentation link), not a panic or a black screen
Given Windows 11 x86_64 and macOS 14+ arm64, When the binary runs, Then a window opens and renders the same components

subFeatures.name: Valkey build for Windows & macOS
acceptanceCriteria: Given Valkey 8.x/9.x source, When a CI job runs the CMake build on windows-latest, Then it produces valkey-server.exe that starts, serves PING -> PONG, and shuts down cleanly
Given the macos-latest runner (arm64) and macos-13 (x86_64), When the build runs, Then it produces a binary for both architectures with the same PING result
Given one target fails after a reasonable effort, Then the D-13 fallback activates: Valkey is marked unsupported for that platform in the catalog, the UI shows the reason, and the PRD is updated

subFeatures.name: PostgreSQL lifecycle from the upstream tarball
acceptanceCriteria: Given a theseus-rs 18.x artifact for the runner's platform, When the spike downloads, verifies SHA-256, extracts, runs initdb then pg_ctl start, Then a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:<port> succeeds with SELECT 1
Given the cycle is complete, When pg_ctl stop -m fast is called, Then the process ends in < 5 seconds and no orphaned postgres process remains

subFeatures.name: Tray icon on three OSes alongside GPUI
acceptanceCriteria: Given GPUI has its own event loop, When the tray icon is installed, Then the icon appears on Windows, macOS, and at least one Linux desktop environment (GNOME via AppIndicator, and KDE)
Given the tray menu is clicked, Then the action reaches app state without blocking or breaking the GPUI event loop
Given the tray is unavailable in the user's desktop environment, Then the app still works fully through the window and the missing tray shows as a note, not an error

subFeatures.name: Skeleton workspace & CI matrix
acceptanceCriteria: Given an empty repo, When cargo xtask ci runs locally, Then the workspace (core, gui, cli, xtask) compiles, clippy is clean, and the tests pass
Given a push to main, When the workflow runs, Then the linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-universal, windows-x86_64 matrix produces artifacts and checksums.txt

subFeatures.name: Bundled snapshot + periodic refresh
acceptanceCriteria: Given the app is opened for the first time without an internet connection, When the catalog page is opened, Then the version list from the bundled snapshot still shows with the banner 'The catalog may be out of date'
Given the last snapshot was refreshed more than 24 hours ago and a connection exists, When the app opens, Then the refresh runs in the background and the UI updates without blocking interaction
Given the refresh fails (timeout, 404, GitHub rate limit), Then there is no error dialog; only the catalog status banner changes and the old snapshot stays in use
Given the catalog payload has a schema_version higher than the app understands, Then the payload is rejected, the bundled snapshot stays in use, and the app suggests an update

subFeatures.name: Version list & filter
acceptanceCriteria: Given the catalog loads, When the user opens New Instance, Then only versions with an artifact for this machine's OS+arch are shown
Given an engine has no artifact for this platform, Then the engine stays visible but disabled with a textual reason, not silently hidden
Given a version is already installed as a local runtime, Then that version is marked 'Installed' and creating an instance skips the whole download step

subFeatures.name: Catalog builder pipeline (CI)
acceptanceCriteria: Given a daily scheduled job, When the job runs, Then it queries each engine's upstream source and produces catalog/engines.json
Given a new artifact is found, When the job processes it, Then it fetches the upstream .sha256 file or computes the checksum itself, and refuses to write an entry without a checksum
Given the result differs from the current catalog, Then the job opens a pull request (not a direct push) so catalog changes are always reviewed by a human

subFeatures.name: Resumable download with progress
acceptanceCriteria: Given a 260 MB download is running, When the connection drops and the user presses Resume, Then the download continues with an HTTP Range header from the last byte, not from zero
Given a download is running, Then the UI shows percent, bytes downloaded/total, speed and ETA, updated at least twice per second
Given the server responds 200 rather than 206 (no Range support), Then the app restarts from the beginning transparently, without showing an error
Given the user presses Cancel, Then the download stops in < 1 second and the .part file is deleted

subFeatures.name: Verification & clean failure
acceptanceCriteria: Given the download finishes, When the SHA-256 differs from the catalog value, Then the file is deleted, the install is cancelled, and the message names the expected vs. actual checksum with a Retry button
Given extraction fails midway (disk full, corrupt archive), Then the half-built runtime directory is removed entirely
Given the archive contains a path that escapes the destination directory (../) or an absolute symlink, Then extraction is refused as an unsafe archive (zip-slip protection)

subFeatures.name: Extraction & runtime layout
acceptanceCriteria: Given a .tar.gz, .tar.xz or .zip archive, When it is extracted, Then its contents land in ~/.dblocal/runtimes/<engine>/<version>-<arch>/ with the catalog strip_prefix applied so bin/ sits exactly one level inside
Given a Unix platform, When extraction finishes, Then the executable bit on each file in bin/ is set
Given a runtime already exists for the same version+arch, Then the download is skipped and the status is immediately installed

subFeatures.name: Reclaim disk
acceptanceCriteria: Given a runtime is no longer referenced by any instance, When the user opens Settings -> Storage, Then that runtime is listed as 'Unused' with its size and can be deleted
Given a runtime is still referenced by at least one instance, Then its delete button is disabled with the list of instances using it

subFeatures.name: Automatic allocation
acceptanceCriteria: Given there is no PostgreSQL instance yet, When the user creates a PostgreSQL instance, Then the proposed port is 5432
Given an instance already uses 5432, When the user creates a second PostgreSQL instance, Then the proposed port is 5433 (the next free port)
Given the user types a port already allocated to another DBLocal instance, Then the form refuses to submit and names the owning instance

subFeatures.name: Bind test before start
acceptanceCriteria: Given the instance's port is taken by a process outside DBLocal, When the user presses Start, Then the app detects it through a real bind attempt to 127.0.0.1:<port> before running the engine, and shows a 'Port is already in use' dialog with a one-click 'Move to <port+1>' action
Given the user chooses to move the port, Then the instance configuration is updated, the old allocation is released, and the start continues with no extra steps
Given the bind test succeeds, Then the test socket is closed before the engine runs, so there is no race with the engine process

transitions.trigger: system: port conflict / process died / timeout (30s; Valkey 10s)

subFeatures.name: Create an instance
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user picks an engine + version and presses Create, When the required runtime is already installed, Then the instance is created in status stopped in < 10 seconds with no question beyond the name (pre-filled with a default)
Given the runtime is not installed, Then the flow continues automatically to F-RTM with visible progress, then returns to initialization without user interaction
Given the instance name is taken, Then the form refuses and suggests an alternative name

subFeatures.name: Initialize the data directory
acceptanceCriteria: Given a new PostgreSQL instance, When initialization runs, Then initdb is called with UTF-8 encoding, C.UTF-8 locale, and the authentication method matching the auth mode (scram-sha-256 or trust)
Given a new Valkey instance, Then valkey.conf is written with bind 127.0.0.1, port, dir, and requirepass when the auth mode has a password
Given initialization fails, Then the data directory is cleaned up entirely and the raw engine tool output is shown in the log panel, not summarized as 'an error occurred'
Given any platform, Then every engine is configured to listen on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 only, never 0.0.0.0

subFeatures.name: Start / Stop
acceptanceCriteria: Given a stopped instance, When the user presses Start, Then the F-PRT-02 bind test runs, the engine is spawned detached, and the status becomes running after the health check passes
Given a running instance and the user quits the app fully, When the app is opened again, Then the instance is still running and still controllable
Given a running instance, When the user presses Stop, Then clean shutdown is called and the status becomes stopped in < 20 seconds; past that, a forced kill runs and is recorded
Given the engine process dies on its own, When the app detects it (poll <= 2 seconds), Then the status becomes failed and the last 20 log lines are shown without being asked

subFeatures.name: Reconcile orphaned processes
acceptanceCriteria: Given the app starts and a pidfile exists from a previous session, When reconciliation runs, Then each PID is verified as really our engine process by matching the executable name and process start time against the recorded values
Given a PID has been reused by another process that does not match, Then the pidfile is treated as stale, deleted, and the instance marked stopped - the app never signals a foreign process
Given reconciliation for 20 instances, Then it all finishes in < 2 seconds and does not block the window render

subFeatures.name: Delete an instance
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user presses Delete, Then the dialog shows the data dir size and two actions: 'Delete instance and data' and 'Delete instance, keep data'
Given the user chooses 'Delete instance and data', Then the confirm button becomes enabled only after the user types the instance name exactly

Given the user chooses 'Delete instance, keep data', Then the data directory is moved to ~/.dblocal/archive/<name>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>/, the instance entry is deleted, the port allocation is released, and the keychain credential is deleted
Given the instance is running, Then Delete stops it first and fails cleanly if the stop fails

subFeatures.name: Generate & store credentials
acceptanceCriteria: Given a new instance with the password auth mode, When it is created, Then a 24-character password is generated from the OS CSPRNG and stored in the keychain under the key dblocal:<instance-id>
Given the keychain is unavailable, Then the 0600 file fallback is used and the UI shows the note 'Stored in a file, not the keychain' with its path
Given an instance is deleted, Then its keychain/file entry is deleted too

subFeatures.name: Copy the connection URI
acceptanceCriteria: Given a running instance, When the user presses Copy URI, Then the clipboard holds a complete, valid URI (e.g. postgresql://postgres:<password>@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres) and a confirmation toast appears
Given a Valkey instance, Then the URI is redis://default:<password>@127.0.0.1:6379
Given the user presses Copy .env, Then the clipboard holds a framework-style environment variable block (DB_CONNECTION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_DATABASE, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD)
Given the password contains characters that need escaping in a URI, Then the password is percent-encoded correctly so the URI can always be parsed

subFeatures.name: No-password mode
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user checks 'Allow connections without a password' at create time, Then a warning dialog explains that other processes and users on this machine can connect without credentials, and the user must confirm once more
Given this mode is active, Then the instance card shows a permanent 'No auth' badge
Given a Valkey engine with this mode, Then protected-mode yes is still kept in the config

subFeatures.name: Per-instance log panel
acceptanceCriteria: Given an instance has been started, When the user opens the Logs tab, Then the last 1000 lines are shown and new lines stream live while the instance is running
Given the log file exceeds 10 MB, Then the log is rotated (.1, .2, at most 3 files) so the disk does not grow without bound
Given the user presses Copy logs, Then the last 500 lines go to the clipboard, to paste into a GitHub issue

subFeatures.name: Start-failure diagnosis
acceptanceCriteria: Given a start failed, When the app shows the failure, Then the message maps a known cause to an action: port in use -> 'Change port'; data dir from another engine version -> 'Version mismatch, a new instance is required'; permission denied -> the offending path; binary missing/corrupt -> 'Reinstall the runtime'

Given an unrecognized cause, Then the app shows the last relevant raw log line + a 'Report an issue' button with a filled-in template (OS, architecture, app version, engine, engine version) without the password or an identifying home path

subFeatures.name: Tray menu
acceptanceCriteria: Given the app is running, Then the tray/menubar icon shows the instance list with status dots (green running, grey stopped, red failed) and allows start/stop directly from the menu
Given an instance is changed from the tray menu, Then the main window (when open) reflects the change within <= 1 second
Given the tray is unsupported in the user's desktop environment, Then the app still works fully through the window and shows the note once

subFeatures.name: Close & quit behavior
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user closes the window, Then the app stays alive in the tray and instances keep running
Given the user chooses Quit while instances are running, Then the dialog offers 'Leave them running' (default) or 'Stop all, then quit'
Given the user chooses 'Leave them running', Then the engine processes stay alive after the app exits and F-INS-04 reconnects them when the app is opened again

subFeatures.name: Build matrix & checksum
acceptanceCriteria: Given a v* tag is pushed, Then CI produces artifacts for linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-universal, windows-x86_64 plus checksums.txt
Given an artifact exceeds the 60 MB size limit, Then the build fails (size gate) rather than passing silently

subFeatures.name: Portable artifacts (AppImage, tar.gz, dmg, zip)
acceptanceCriteria: Given a Phase 1 release, Then .AppImage and .tar.gz (Linux), a notarized .dmg (macOS universal), and .zip (Windows) are available
Given the AppImage runs on Fedora and the latest Ubuntu LTS, Then the app opens with no extra dependencies beyond the system Vulkan driver
Given the .dmg is downloaded through a browser on macOS, Then the app opens without any terminal command

subFeatures.name: install.sh for curl
acceptanceCriteria: Given curl -fsSL <url>/install.sh | sh runs on Linux or macOS, Then the script detects OS+arch, downloads the right artifact, verifies the checksum, installs to ~/.local/bin (or /usr/local/bin when writable), and prints the next step
Given an unsupported architecture, Then the script stops with a clear message and installs nothing
Given the script is run again, Then it performs an idempotent in-place upgrade
Given CI, Then the script passes shellcheck and never calls sudo without an explicit flag

subFeatures.name: Native packages (.deb, .rpm, .msi)
acceptanceCriteria: Given a Phase 2 release, Then .deb (Debian/Ubuntu), .rpm (Fedora/RHEL), and .msi (Windows) are available
Given .deb/.rpm is installed and then removed, Then no files are left behind outside ~/.dblocal, and the fact that user data is kept is stated at uninstall time

subFeatures.name: Self-update
acceptanceCriteria: Given a newer version is available on GitHub Releases, When the user opens Settings -> Updates, Then the new version + release notes are shown with an install button
Given the app was installed through the OS package manager, Then self-update is disabled and the app points the user to their package manager
Given the Windows platform, Then the update uses a helper process that replaces the binary after the app exits
Given the update package, Then the checksum is verified before installing

subFeatures.name: MySQL adapter
acceptanceCriteria: Given a MySQL artifact from the catalog, When an instance is created, Then initialization uses mysqld --initialize-insecure, then the superuser password is set and my.cnf is written with bind-address=127.0.0.1, port, and the instance datadir
Given a running instance, Then the health check uses the MySQL protocol handshake, not just a process check
Given a 260 MB download, Then progress and ETA are shown from the first byte and the download can be resumed after a drop

subFeatures.name: MariaDB adapter
acceptanceCriteria: Given a MariaDB artifact from downloads.mariadb.org/rest-api, When an instance is created, Then initialization uses mariadb-install-db with --auth-root-authentication-method=normal
Given MariaDB and MySQL are both installed, Then they appear as different engines with different canonical ports (3306 vs 3307) and never share a data dir

subFeatures.name: Manage databases
acceptanceCriteria: Given a running instance, When the user opens the Databases tab, Then the database list with sizes is shown
Given the user creates a new database with a valid name, Then the database is created with UTF-8 encoding (utf8mb4_unicode_ci for the MySQL family) and appears in the list immediately
Given the user deletes a database, Then the confirmation requires typing the database name
Given a name contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_], Then the form rejects it before any command is sent to the engine

subFeatures.name: Manage users & privileges
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user creates a new database user, Then they can choose the database and the privilege level (read-only or read-write), and the matching GRANT command is run
Given the user is created, Then its password is shown once and stored in the keychain like the superuser credential

subFeatures.name: Reset the superuser password
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user presses Reset password, Then a new password is generated, applied to the engine, stored in the keychain, and the displayed URI is updated with it
Given the reset fails midway, Then the old password stays in effect and the keychain is unchanged

subFeatures.name: Detect installed clients
acceptanceCriteria: Given the machine has DBDelve, TablePlus, DBeaver, or a CLI (psql, mysql, valkey-cli/redis-cli), When the user opens the 'Open in...' menu, Then only clients actually detected are shown
Given none is detected, Then the menu shows 'Copy URI' instead, not an empty list

subFeatures.name: Open with the instance connection
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user picks a GUI client, Then the client opens directly on that instance's connection (URL scheme when available, or command-line arguments)

Given the user picks a CLI client, Then the OS terminal opens with a ready-to-run command, and the password is supplied through environment variables (PGPASSWORD, MYSQL_PWD), not as an argument visible in the process list

subFeatures.name: Inspection (list, status)
acceptanceCriteria: Given several instances exist, When dblocal list runs, Then a name/engine/version/port/status table is printed; --json produces pipeable JSON
Given dblocal status <name>, Then the instance status is printed with exit code 0 when running and non-zero otherwise

subFeatures.name: Control (start, stop)
acceptanceCriteria: Given dblocal start <name>, Then the command blocks until the health check passes or times out, then exits with the matching code
Given the GUI is open while the CLI changes state, Then the GUI reflects the change within <= 2 seconds
Given two processes try to start the same instance at once, Then one wins and the other exits with the message 'already running', guaranteed by the SQLite transaction

subFeatures.name: Lifecycle & URI
acceptanceCriteria: Given dblocal uri <name>, Then the connection URI is printed to stdout with no decoration so it can be piped straight into .env
Given dblocal create --engine postgresql --version 18.7 --name app-dev, Then the instance is created non-interactively, downloading the runtime when needed, and the URI is printed when done
Given dblocal delete <name>, Then the delete refuses to run without --yes in a non-interactive session, and by default archives the data rather than deleting it

subFeatures.name: Form for key settings
acceptanceCriteria: Given a PostgreSQL instance, When the user opens the Config tab, Then the form shows the high-value subset (port, max_connections, shared_buffers, work_mem, timezone, authentication method) with current and default values
Given the user saves changes, Then the app states that a restart is required and offers to do it now
Given a change makes the engine fail to start, Then the app offers 'Restore the previous configuration' from a copy saved before the change

subFeatures.name: Edit the raw file
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user chooses 'Open config file', Then the file opens in the OS default text editor, and comments and lines the app does not recognize are never rewritten or deleted by the app

subFeatures.name: App autostart at login
acceptanceCriteria: Given the user enables 'Run at login', Then a login item is registered through the appropriate user-level mechanism (systemd --user, LaunchAgent, Registry Run) without sudo
Given the option is turned off, Then that entry is removed entirely
Given the app is started by the login item, Then it opens straight to the tray without showing a window

subFeatures.name: Autostart selected instances
acceptanceCriteria: Given an instance is flagged for autostart, When the app starts at login, Then that instance is started and the result is visible in the tray
Given one instance's autostart fails, Then the failure does not block other instances and shows no modal dialog; a failed status in the tray and window is enough

subFeatures.name: Full keyboard navigation
acceptanceCriteria: Given only a keyboard, Then the whole first-session flow (pick engine -> create -> start -> copy URI) can be completed, with focus always visible
Given the command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K), Then the user can search instances and run start/stop/copy URI

subFeatures.name: Theme & contrast
acceptanceCriteria: Given a light or dark system theme, Then the app follows it and all text meets a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1
Given an instance status, Then status is never conveyed by colour alone (there is always a text label or accompanying icon)

entities.name: Engine
entities.lifecycle: static, changes with an app release

entities.name: EngineVersion
entities.lifecycle: refreshed from the catalog; old entries kept while a runtime still uses them

entities.name: Runtime
entities.lifecycle: hard delete through F-RTM-04, only when unreferenced

entities.name: Instance
entities.lifecycle: hard delete with the option to archive the data dir

entities.name: PortAllocation
entities.lifecycle: released when an instance is deleted or its port changes

entities.name: CredentialRef
entities.lifecycle: deleted with the instance; the secret lives in the keychain, not the DB

entities.name: ArchivedData
entities.lifecycle: deleted only by hand through Settings -> Storage

entities.name: CatalogSnapshot
entities.lifecycle: one active row, replaced on refresh

metrics.name: Sukses install engine
metrics.verify: E2E job per OS on every release

metrics.name: Install-failure issue rate
metrics.verify: public proxy, counted by hand per release

decisions.title: Primary user: a multi-project web developer who rejects Docker
First-session job: one running instance + a copied connection URI in < 2 minutes
Core value: multi-version native, one click, no container
Retention through tray + autostart
Free and open source under GPL-3.0-only, no telemetry, no license key
UI uses GPUI + gpui-component (Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0 compatible); DBDelve code is not copied, as an engineering decision
App state in SQLite (WAL)
Distribution through GitHub Releases + install.sh + self-update
Zero sudo at runtime
Engine processes detached; the app is only a controller
CLI in Phase 2, UI-agnostic core crate from Phase 1
Engine binaries downloaded from upstream, guided by our own JSON catalog
Valkey as the Redis-compatible engine, with a mandatory Windows spike
Four engines in v1: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Valkey
v1 scope = core + DB/user management + open-in-client + config editor
Canonical port then auto-increment, with a real bind test
Random per-instance password in the OS keychain; optional no-password mode
Deleting an instance offers delete-data or archive
Bundled catalog + 24-hour TTL refresh; resumable downloads
macOS notarized; Windows unsigned in v1
Phase order: P0 spikes, P1 PostgreSQL+Valkey, P2 MySQL/MariaDB+CLI+packages, P3 configuration+autostart
Product name DBLocal, binary dblocal, data in ~/.dblocal/
Zed IDE-style UI (dock, tabbed panes, status bar, command palette); dark+light themes from the One Dark/Light palette; colour tokens must pass 4.5:1 contrast
decisions.supersedes: the DBDelve look reference in D-06

decisions.title: Per-platform engine support follows the real upstream artifacts (MariaDB only Linux x86_64 and Windows x64; Valkey only Linux; MySQL Linux x86_64 uses the 80 MB minimal tarball); MySQL SHA-256 is computed by CI

openQuestions.question: Can Valkey be built for Windows (and macOS) in CI with a stable result?
openQuestions.gate: F-SPK-02; if not, the D-13 fallback applies and five-OS parity breaks

openQuestions.question: Can a tray icon be integrated with the GPUI event loop on three OSes?
openQuestions.gate: F-SPK-04; if not, the D-04 retention trigger must be replaced

openQuestions.question: How mature is GPUI on Windows for non-Zed apps, and how often does gpui-pre introduce breaking changes?
Who owns the Apple Developer account, who pays the fee, and how is the signing secret stored in GitHub Actions?
Is the linux-aarch64 runner available and stable, or does the arm64 build need cross-compilation/QEMU?
Is the name DBLocal free of conflicts on crates.io, the Homebrew cask, winget, and as a domain?
Which MySQL download endpoint is stable for automation, and do its terms allow programmatic downloads?

assumptions.text: theseus-rs/postgresql-binaries stays maintained and keeps releasing new PostgreSQL versions (currently 18.7.0)
assumptions.mitigation: the catalog is data, so the source can be switched without changing code

assumptions.text: The Valkey tarball for Ubuntu jammy runs on Fedora thanks to glibc backward compatibility
assumptions.mitigation: proven by the Fedora E2E job in Phase 1

assumptions.text: The target user runs a machine with a working Vulkan driver
assumptions.mitigation: a clear message for a machine without Vulkan, not a crash

assumptions.text: A 260 MB download for MySQL is acceptable as long as progress, ETA and resume are shown
Keychain is available in the majority of target desktop environments; the 0600 file fallback is enough for the rest
There are no additional legal obligations because no personal data is collected
assumptions.mitigation: reviewed again if opt-in telemetry is considered

backlog: Adopting an existing database install on the machine
